'''Operation Domino''' was a disastrous operation made by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during their initial struggles against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

==Prelude==
Soon after the [[Declaration of Rebellion/Legends|Declaration of Rebellion]], the [[Alliance Military/Legends|Alliance Military]] was organized in [[Sector Force/Legends|Sector Forces]]. Operation Domino was the first campaign of the Rebel Alliance against the Empire. The operation was planned, among others, by [[Chief of State (Alliance)/Legends|Chief of State]] [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]]. Its premise was to call in the stronger Sector Forces to defeat local Imperial [[Garrison/Legends|garrisons]] in showpiece battles and then dig in behind their [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shields]] with the intention of proving that planets could free themselves and thus inspire revolution across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="TEGtW" />

==The campaign==
Operation Domino backfired in that it caused the various uprisings to meet crushing defeat. The planets that revolted were branded the "[[Secession Worlds]]" by the Empire and they were quickly crushed by the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]]. The result for the Rebellion was no mass revolution, instead resulting in a dozens of Alliance armies destroyed, and surviving units fleeing. Mon Mothma learned that while having a hundred Sector Forces would muster infantry [[Brigade/Legends|brigades]], it was only part of an army that most of the soldiers lacked formal training, while some lacking even bases, and others lacked air support or spare parts.<ref name="TEGtW" />

One of the few rebel victories of the campaign was the [[Calamarian Revolt|liberation]] of [[Dac/Legends|Dac]].<ref name="TEGtW" />

==Aftermath==
In spite of the military disaster, Operation Domino also had unexpected good results. The sacrifice of the rebels created a wave of sympathy for the Rebellion, and more particularly from the ranks of the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]. Many top [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]] such as [[General/Legends|General]] [[Kryll]] and [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Harles]] defected mid-campaign. They helped the reorganization of the battered rebel brigades into what became the [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|Alliance Special Forces]].<ref name="TEGtW" />

The [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] were also freed during this campaign. Having thrown off Imperial rule, the Calamari [[Space mine/Legends|mined]] the approaches to their [[Calamari sector/Legends|sector]], which would become an essential redoubt and source of [[Starship/Legends|starships]] for the Rebellion.<ref name="TEGtW" />

==Behind the scenes==
According to Paul Urquhart in Jason Fry's endnotes of ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'', the name of the campaign was derived from the "[[Wikipedia:Domino theory|domino theory]]," a theory dating back to the Vietnam War-era regarding the likelihood that Communism will run rampant across Southeast Asia and other regions if left unchecked. He also noted that the event itself was first mentioned in the ''Rebel Alliance'' sourcebook, although he isn't sure if the name came from the source or if he named it himself.<ref name="JLT">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/24881617404/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-11|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 11}}</ref> Coincidentally, the Rebel Alliance themselves had been modeled after the Vietcong in Vietnam, which were one of the elements the domino theory warned about.<ref name="New York Post">{{WebCite|url=https://nypost.com/2014/09/21/how-star-wars-was-secretly-george-lucas-protest-of-vietnam|text=How 'Star Wars' was secretly George Lucas' Vietnam protest|author=Kyle Smith|date=2014-10-21|work=New York Post|archivedate=20180826122931}}</ref><ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.yomyomf.com/star-wars-is-a-metaphor-for-the-vietcong-kicking-american-ass-in-the-vietnam-war|text='Star Wars' is a Metaphor for the Vietcong Kicking American Ass in the Vietnam War?|date=2015-12-16|archivedate=20160610224959}}</ref>
